content.thinking:
I need to write this carefully in one pass since I can't test it, keeping things robust with solid geometric construction, lathes, extrusions, sweeps, and surface treatments. I'm planning a workbench roughly 1.8m by 0.8m with a 0.9m tall tabletop, and thinking through whether plain objects still need a root joint structure since the builder requires exactly one root joint.

I'll set up a single root joint at the origin so parts without explicit bones attach there correctly. The design calls for a tabletop around 0.9m with shelving above holding bottles up to about 1.5m, staying within a 64-color budget by relying mostly on paint fills rather than flat colors. For the table itself I'm planning a wood-finished top with legs, stretchers, gilded trim, drawer fronts with knobs, and a decorative cloth runner with an alchemical circle pattern laid flat across the surface.

On top of the table I'm arranging several object groups: a stack of books with cream page blocks and gilt-trimmed covers plus an open book with tilted text-filled pages; a brass balance scale built from lathe parts, a beam, chain rods, and small weight cylinders; glowing potion flasks made from lathe liquid cores with pale glass necks and corks, alongside a rack of gold-capped vials; and I'm continuing to plan out additional decorative elements for the scene.

I'm also designing a mortar and pestle, hanging herb bundles tied to a rail above the table, and a tall wooden shelf unit behind it holding more bottles and books on two levels. For finishing touches I'm adding a glowing candle, a crystal cluster, a small lantern, golden tassels, and a cauldron resting on the floor beside the table.

Setting up box, cylinder, and lathe helper functions for constructing the scene geometry...

Still writing the flask lathe outline...

Then I'll make a parametrized potion function covering flask, vial, and square bottle types, and a book helper for bookshelf items with cover boxes and inset page blocks, varying colors and spine decals like gold bands.

I'll add gold spine bands at a few heights, then think about color budget—using cel paints for bigger surfaces like wood and the table/shelf/rug, and flat colors for small items to keep total colors around 60 or under. Now I'm planning the SVG textures, starting with a runner texture sized to fit the table proportions.

Writing SVG code...

Working through the basis orientation for the plane's local axes so the texture reads upright from the front viewer's perspective, checking the cross products to confirm the default orientation works without needing a custom up vector.

For the open book layout, I'm planning to build it from a cover box plus two page boxes, each with a texture plane on top tilted slightly (around 4 degrees on the z-axis) to suggest pages fanning open, applying rotation directly to the planes rather than using the dir-based orientation.

Confirming the rotateX(-90°) math checks out for the plane's normal direction. For hanging herbs, I'm planning card-based bundles with leaf textures, double-sided frames facing up, and string ties, using the imported frame helper for positioning.

The sprig texture should draw with stem at the bottom of the image so it reads correctly when hung upside-down (root at top, leaves hanging down). I'm also sketching potted plants (standing cards with fan-leaf textures and spin), plus a mortar and pestle setup -- a lathe-turned stone bowl, an angled pestle rod, and flat green herb cards inside the bowl.

Now for a scale: I'm placing it at roughly (-0.55, 0.9, 0.05) with a lathe-turned base, a vertical column, a beam at the top, a pivot sphere, and thin rods connecting beam ends down to shallow lathe-bowl pans. I'm keeping the beam level but varying what's in each pan (herbs on one side, weights on the other) rather than tilting it, to keep things simple and balanced-looking.

For the shelf unit behind the table, I'm working out a back panel positioned around z=-0.36 spanning the table width, with two shelf boards at different heights and a depth that keeps them within the available table space.

Now I'm adding corner posts rising from the floor at the back corners up to about 1.8 units tall, plus a top crossbeam and a hanging rail where herbs can dangle from a rod spanning the width.

I'm adjusting shelf heights to around 1.15 and 1.42 so herb growth and shelf items don't collide, and repositioning the hanging rail further forward so herbs drape in front of the back panel instead of overlapping other objects.

I'm spacing out the herb bundles along the crossbeam and checking scale heights don't clash with them, then adding a glowing crystal cluster and candles on the table. For the table itself, I'm setting dimensions at 1.8 by 0.8 centered at origin, placing legs symmetrically, and adding a lower shelf for crates or jars.

Now I'm working out the front apron with three drawers, each with gold knobs, keyhole plates, and trim frames, positioning them just proud of the apron surface near the top edge. I'm also considering adding a small tassel hanging beneath the apron for extra detail but may skip the full cloth runner to keep things simpler.

Now I'm defining the flat color palette as named constants—gold, gold-dark, teal, teal-dark, cream, paper, red, purple, blue, green, pink—so I can reference them consistently across all the painted wood and decorative elements.

I'm setting up grain-textured paint helpers for wood and dark wood, specifying grain direction along the table top versus the legs, and accounting for shadow resolution on these cel-shaded materials.

Now I'm starting to compose the actual SVG strings for each asset, like the runner rune design with a teal background, gold border, dashed inner line, central circle and triangle motifs, and small rune glyphs, making sure stroke widths stay visible at the target raster resolution before moving to the next texture piece like the book cover top.

Still sketching more elements...

RUG continues as maroon with gold pattern border and diamond center at 512 size. Now I'm moving into actually writing the component code, being careful with TypeScript types for the lathe outline points, making sure arrays are properly typed as OutlinePoint[] so the helper functions accept them correctly.

Working out the flask outline and liquid fill coordinates...

I'm noticing the neck glass radius risks overlapping with the liquid outline near the shoulder, so I should simplify by treating the whole flask as one continuous outline rather than separate liquid and glass pieces.

Working out the neck and cork lathe coordinates...

I'm setting up a glow helper for flat-colored parts, and planning a potion-building function. For books, I need rotation around the Y axis, so I'm working out a local-to-world placement function that applies standard 2D rotation math to offset coordinates for each book part.

Then I'm designing a lying-book-stack builder: covers as boxes with inset page blocks visible on three sides, and a spine piece on the opposite side, parameterized by length, thickness, depth, color and band accent.

I'm structuring the book as separate boards (top, bottom, spine) around a recessed pages block, plus gold trim details on the cover and spine. Then I'm placing a stack of three flat books on the table, each slightly rotated with varying thickness, length, and color.

Now I'm adding a glowing crystal cluster made from stretched octahedrons sitting atop the book stack and in a table corner. For the open book in the center-left, I'm building a cover box plus two tilted page blocks rotated slightly about the z-axis so the inner edges dip downward realistically.

To fix the small offset error, I'll translate the plane geometry upward before rotating it, so it stays correctly aligned at the block's center. I'm also planning a glass quill and inkwell nearby—the inkwell as a lathed shape, and the quill as a rod from the inkwell with a feather extruded as a flat outline shape.

For the feather, I'll skip a complex extrusion and instead use a sphere geometry scaled thin and oriented along the direction axis, which is simpler. For the mortar, I'm sketching a lathe profile for the stone bowl with an outer hollow and inner wall contour.

Inside the bowl I'm adding flattened green herb spheres, and a pestle made from a tapered rod with a rounded pommel end, positioned tip-down into the bowl. For the candle, I'm planning a cream cylinder with drips, a lathed wax dish, and a glowing flame built from a small cone plus an inner glow layer, sitting in a gold candle holder dish.

Lower shelf holds lathed jars with lids and a couple of banded barrels. Beside the table I'm placing an iron cauldron on three legs with a glowing green disc inside for contents, floating bubble spheres, and a torus handle, which widens the overall prop bounds. I'm also adding a crate with slats, straw, and a few potion bottles on the right side, plus a rug beneath the whole setup.

Now I'm layering the rug as a thin maroon box with a textured plane just above it, keeping the lowest point flush with the floor. For the Genshin-inspired palette I want gold filigree trim, so I'm generating a repeating gold spiral-and-scroll SVG pattern on a dark teal background to apply to the apron front.

Writing filigree SVG paths...

I'm now working out apron proportions—placing the drawer fronts, aligning the filigree strip above the apron, and adjusting the table top and apron y-ranges so everything fits together without overlapping the tabletop.

I settle on a filigree band 1.62x0.08 at y 0.79 with a texture viewBox sized so circles render cleanly, and drawer fronts centered at y 0.68 with the apron bottom at 0.62. With the proportions planned out, I'm ready to write the code carefully, making sure to use all imports and avoid unused locals under strict TypeScript settings.

I decide on grain and mottle texture helpers alongside the paint utilities, pulling in frame, rng, and cel/INK for the SVG ink styling, and I set up a small helper function to shorten repeated part-creation calls.

Still writing geometry helpers...

I'll annotate the map callback explicitly to avoid type inference issues, then move on to wiring up the glow effect for lathe parts and a label plane using a texture. Next I'm sketching a helper for placing books standing in a row on shelves.

Now I'm cycling through a potion color palette and laying out the tabletop scene: a runner cloth under the items, a stack of books with a crystal on top, an open book to the side, and an inkwell with quill nearby, all positioned relative to the table surface height.

I'm placing the remaining props — a balance scale with pans checked against the open book's edge so they don't overlap, then a cluster of potion vessels including a flask, a small vial rack, a square bottle, and a mortar, each positioned and sized to fit around the open book's footprint without colliding.

Adjusting the stack to x 0.7 with varied lengths, keeping bottles left of 0.42. I'm placing a potted plant front-right and an herb bundle with loose leaves front-left on the table, then laying out shelf positions with bottom and top shelves spanning the width at different depths.

For shelf contents, I'm putting books and bottles on the bottom shelf and adding a glowing crystal orb on a gold stand as the centerpiece of the top shelf alongside more books and bottles. For the back panel, I'm keeping it simple with painted wood grain and vertical plank lines rather than adding extra decorative elements.

Now I'm positioning the support posts at the back corners, adjusting their width so they sit flush with the table legs and back panel edges, widening the table top slightly to accommodate the overlap, and adding a cross beam box across the top to connect the posts structurally.

Adding a center gem and positioning the crest, then sketching out the arms and rail connecting the posts—boxes and a thin rod spanning between them at the right height.

Now I'm working on the herb bundles hanging from the rail: small cords tying groups of cards that fan out, with each card's facing direction controlled by a flow and spin variation rather than a simple downward lean.

Adjusting sprig size to reach 1.48, then setting up card frames for the bundles at seven x-positions, each with four cards using randomized leaf/lavender/flower textures across the mesh. I'll skip hanging garlic strings and just have potted plants with leaning cards, double-sided, no cross pattern.

For potted plants, I'm arranging leaf-fan textured frames in a ring around the pot, oriented outward with a 40-degree lean to fan them nicely. Now I'm shaping the cauldron with a lathe profile, defining the curved iron outline point by point.

Adding the glowing green liquid disc inside the cauldron, interpolating the inner wall radius at that height, then sketching bubbles, simple rod handles, and small glowing orange flame cones tucked between the legs underneath.

Now I'm placing the cauldron at its final table position with clearance checked against the post, then moving on to the crate of potions nearby — building it from corner posts and side planks, filling it with straw, bottles, and a tied sack of herbs sitting on top.

I'm sizing the overall room so the rug stays centered and covers most of the floor without overlapping the cauldron, then working out a lower shelf beneath the table to hold a barrel, jars, and a stack of books.

For the barrel itself, I'm lathing a staved profile and adding thin cylindrical bands at a couple of heights, sizing the band radii just slightly larger than the barrel's curve so they sit flush, and keeping the segment count consistent between the lathe and bands for a clean match.

Now I'm adding jars with lids and corks, finishing the drawer fronts, and including a stretcher between the legs to serve as a lower shelf. For painting, I'm grouping wood tones into a few named palettes—main wood, vertical-grain wood, and dark wood for posts/shelves—and using flat colors for small trim pieces to keep the total paint/texture count manageable, aiming to stay under roughly fifty flat colors overall. Next I'll write the candle flame geometry and then move into the full object code, making sure the frame import and any embedded SVG text are properly closed and valid.

Writing rug/runner SVG...

Writing book helper functions...

Still working out the page inset math and spine trim boxes, then double-checking the rotation sign convention before adding a flat textured plane on top.

Now I'm sketching a standing book function that builds cover boards, pages, and trim with spine facing forward, making sure the top emblem orientation reads correctly from the viewer's side.

Still writing book parts...

Then I'm thinking through a simple potion rack design: a base board with vials standing on it and a raised top board supported by two end posts, keeping the piece count manageable.

Still building geometry...

Still building the scale structure...

Pan shape checks out as non-intersecting, with herbs sphere on one side and stacked weight cylinders plus a crystal on the other, chains attaching at the rim via three angled points. I'm now adding the table top with wood box geometry plus a thin gold trim along the front edge, keeping T=0.9 consistent throughout.

Adding legs, foot caps, and apron geometry...

Adding side stretchers between legs, then placing the barrel, jars, and lying books with their positions. I'm mentally checking types for glow fills, then moving to finalize the card objects and texture variations like mottling for wood and stone surfaces before writing the complete code.

Writing part helper function...
